title: Feedback log lives at .rcf/feedback/ and is gitignored
context: Raw feedback entries are written before redaction runs and may hold absolute paths, hostnames and pasted error output. The store is per-clone and per-person, like rcf/.identity/ and .rcf/preflight-secrets.local.json, both already gitignored through the managed block.
decision: The store lives under .rcf/feedback/ and is added to the managed gitignore aggregator via src/feedback/store.js:feedbackGitignoreEntry. src/setup/managed-gitignore.js:managedGitignoreEntries() imports it. rcf feedback add refuses on a project whose .gitignore does not cover the path unless --force is passed, printing the rcf doctor --fix line.
consequences: Unredacted content cannot ride a git push, even accidentally. Existing projects need a rcf doctor --fix (or a rcf init on a fresh clone) to pick up the ignore entry. The shareable, durable record is the GitHub issue; the outbox bundle exists for cases where that record could not be made.

alternativesConsidered.name: Commit rcf/feedback/ so a team can see it
alternativesConsidered.summary: Store entries under the committed rcf/ tree so any team member can browse the log.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Leaks a public-repo user's unredacted findings on the next push, which is the exact failure the redaction step exists to prevent.
